history_page.title: Piano History & Encyclopedia
history_page.heroSubtitle: Discover the evolutionary history from the Harpsichord to modern Grand Pianos, master craftsmanship, and legendary piano brands.

hero.title: Music Theory Foundations &
hero.subtitle: Master clefs (Treble/Bass), note values, accidentals, time signatures (2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8), and interactive chord/scale finder with standard fingerings.

history.title: History & Evolution of the Piano
history.subtitle: From classical stringed instruments to the King of Musical Instruments
history.cristofori_desc: In Florence, Italy, Cristofori created the 'Un cimbalo di cipresso di piano e forte' – allowing players to produce soft (piano) or loud (forte) dynamics via touch intensity.
history.fortepiano_desc: Composers like Mozart, Haydn, and Beethoven wrote masterpieces for the Fortepiano, driving key range expansion and hammer action responsiveness.
history.industrial_desc: Single-piece cast-iron frames and felt-compressed hammers enabled pianos to withstand massive string tension, delivering powerful acoustic projection in concert halls.
history.modern_desc: The pinnacle of Concert Grands combined with Digital and Hybrid Pianos, bringing piano music to millions around the globe.

types.title: Piano Classifications & Characteristics
types.subtitle: Explore the diversity of architectural designs and sound generation mechanics

grand.name: Grand Piano (Horizontal)
grand.desc: Strings and soundboard lie horizontally. Gravity-assisted hammer mechanism allows ultra-fast repetition and ultimate dynamic expression.
grand.feature1: Length ranges from 1.5m (Baby Grand) to 2.7m+ (Concert Grand).
grand.feature2: Lid opens up to project rich acoustic resonance.

upright.name: Upright Piano (Vertical)
upright.desc: Strings and soundboard run vertically. Space-saving elegant design, ideal for homes and music classrooms.
upright.feature2: Compact footprint while preserving true mechanical touch.

digital.name: Digital Piano
digital.desc: Uses audio sampling or physical modeling from world-class concert grands. Features headphone support, USB MIDI, and computer connectivity.
digital.feature1: Weighted action keybed simulates authentic feel.
digital.feature2: No tuning required, easy recording and silent night practice.

hybrid.name: Hybrid Piano (Acoustic-Digital)
hybrid.desc: Combines a real 100% wooden acoustic action with high-precision optical electronic sensors.
hybrid.feature2: Adjustable volume or silent headphone playing.

craftsmanship.title: Anatomy & Craftsmanship Marvels
craftsmanship.subtitle: Over 8,000 precision mechanical parts harmonizing to produce acoustic perfection
craftsmanship.frame_desc: A single-piece cast-iron frame withstands up to 20 tons of string tension across 230+ steel strings.
craftsmanship.soundboard_desc: Crafted from aged Sitka Spruce, acting as the acoustic amplifier heart of the instrument.
craftsmanship.action_desc: Over 8,000 parts made of wood, felt, and leather calibrated to sub-millimeter precision.
craftsmanship.pedal_sustain: Sustain (Right): Lifts all dampers to allow strings to vibrate freely.
craftsmanship.pedal_sostenuto: Sostenuto (Middle): Sustains only the notes currently held down when pressed.
craftsmanship.pedal_soft: Una Corda / Soft (Left): Shifts action so hammers strike fewer strings for a softer tone.

brands.title: Legendary World-Class Piano Makers
brands.subtitle: Icons of musical heritage, uncompromising quality, and artistic excellence

steinway.name: Steinway & Sons
steinway.desc: The gold standard of world concert halls. Chosen by over 95% of concert grand soloists worldwide for its powerful, warm tone and responsive keybed.

bosendorfer.name: Bösendorfer
bosendorfer.desc: Renowned for its rich, singing Viennese tone. The Imperial 290 model features 97 keys (9 extra bass keys).

bechstein.name: C. Bechstein
bechstein.desc: Favored by Liszt and Debussy. Known for clear, singing, aristocratic European tone quality.

fazioli.name: Fazioli
fazioli.desc: The pinnacle of modern artisan craftsmanship. Each Fazioli is custom handcrafted with crystalline acoustic clarity.

yamaha_kawai.name: Yamaha & Kawai
yamaha_kawai.desc: Icons of precision engineering, enduring durability, and global music education contributions.

fundamentals.title: Music Theory Fundamentals & Keyboard
fundamentals.subtitle: Essential building blocks for reading sheet music and mastering the keyboard
fundamentals.staff_desc: Consists of 5 parallel lines and 4 spaces. Higher note positions indicate higher pitches.
fundamentals.clefs_treble: Treble Clef (Sol): Used for higher notes, played with the right hand.
fundamentals.clefs_bass: Bass Clef (Fa): Used for lower notes, played with the left hand.
fundamentals.notes_list: C - D - E - F - G - A - B
fundamentals.keyboard_desc: Comprises 52 white keys and 36 black keys arranged in groups of 2 and 3 black keys.
fundamentals.middle_c_desc: Located directly to the left of the 2-black-key group at the center of the keyboard, serving as the benchmark between Treble and Bass clefs.
fundamentals.interactive_keyboard_subtitle: Click on keys below to listen to pitch sounds, view Hz frequencies, and see note placement on the musical staff.
fundamentals.sharp: Sharp (#): Raises pitch by a semitone (half-step to adjacent right key).
fundamentals.flat: Flat (b): Lowers pitch by a semitone (half-step to adjacent left key).
fundamentals.natural: Natural (♮): Cancels a sharp or flat, returning to natural pitch.
fundamentals.clefs_treble_desc: Higher pitch range, played with the right hand.
fundamentals.clefs_bass_desc: Lower pitch range, played with the left hand.

time_signatures.title: Time Signatures & Rhythm Structure
time_signatures.subtitle: Understanding measure pulses, accents, and beat values (2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8)
time_signatures.top_num_desc: Indicates the exact number of beats in each measure (bar).
time_signatures.bottom_num_desc: Indicates which note value equals one beat (4 = Quarter note, 8 = Eighth note).
time_signatures.ts24_desc: 2 quarter beats per measure. Strong - Weak pulse pattern.
time_signatures.ts34_desc: 3 quarter beats per measure. Strong - Weak - Weak pulse pattern.
time_signatures.ts44_desc: 4 quarter beats per measure. Strong - Weak - Medium - Weak pattern.
time_signatures.ts68_desc: 6 eighth beats divided into 2 groups of 3 (1-2-3, 4-5-6). Flowing ballad rhythm.

chords_scales.title: Piano Chords & Scales Finder
chords_scales.subtitle: Look up chord notes, intervals, finger numbers, and hear live audio playback

major.name: Major
major.desc: Bright and uplifting triad chord, the foundation of classical and modern music.

minor.name: Minor
minor.desc: Melancholic and smooth triad chord featuring a mellow minor third.

dom7.name: Dominant 7th
dom7.desc: Tense bluesy seventh chord that resolves naturally to the tonic.

maj7.name: Major 7th
maj7.desc: Lush and dreamy jazz harmony with an elegant major seventh interval.

min7.name: Minor 7th
min7.desc: Warm, emotional, and versatile chord widely used in Jazz, R&B, and Pop.

dim.name: Diminished
dim.desc: High tension and suspenseful diminished chord composed of minor thirds.

aug.name: Augmented
aug.desc: Dreamlike, floating, and expansive augmented harmony.

sus4.name: Suspended 4th (Sus4)
sus4.desc: Open and suspenseful harmony that replaces the third with a perfect fourth.

major_scale.name: Major Scale
major_scale.desc: Bright, uplifting, and fundamental scale of Western music theory.

natural_minor.name: Natural Minor
natural_minor.desc: Classical minor scale with a somber, emotional tonal color.

harmonic_minor.name: Harmonic Minor
harmonic_minor.desc: Raised 7th degree creating an exotic, dramatic Middle Eastern flavor.

melodic_minor.name: Melodic Minor
melodic_minor.desc: Raised 6th and 7th degrees ascending, widely used in Jazz improvisation.

major_pentatonic.name: Major Pentatonic
major_pentatonic.desc: Traditional Asian folk scale, sweet and very easy to improvise.

minor_pentatonic.name: Minor Pentatonic
minor_pentatonic.desc: The quintessential foundation for Rock, Blues, and Jazz solos.
